subject: Startups
title: Bill Gates and the Software Bet
description: A 60-second lesson on Bill Gates and the Software Bet.

hook.text: In 1975, Bill Gates dropped out of Harvard to write software for a computer he'd never seen in person.

buildup.text: Gates and Paul Allen wrote a BASIC interpreter for the Altair 8800, coding it on a mainframe emulator at Harvard.

discovery.text: Their insight: hardware would become a commodity, but software could be licensed to every machine maker.

twist.text: IBM asked Microsoft for an operating system. Gates bought one for $50,000, tweaked it, and licensed it as MS-DOS.

climax.text: That licensing deal made Microsoft the dominant force in computing for three decades straight.

punchline.text: He bet on software when everyone else bet on hardware.

quiz.question: How did Microsoft get its first operating system for IBM?
options: Bought one for $50,000 and modified it
